assumptions: A 94 × 40 × 68 mm envelope is palm-sized for the requested 14+ desk object.
A single-color opaque filament and ordinary ambient contrast are sufficient for both silhouette reads.

components.form: Fused twin ship-profile skins joined by a broad wave/keel bed, pierced by vertical crescent, whale, and paired blow-jet apertures.
components.interfaces: No assembly interfaces; the two broad perpendicular faces are the stable presentation faces used before and after the quarter-turn.
components.name: Moonwake one-piece body
components.placement: The broad z=0 keel is the print datum; ship profiles occupy the two depth faces and the reveal apertures pass through the bed.
components.purpose: Carry both the sailing-ship outer silhouette and the whale-and-crescent negative-space reveal in one printable solid.

concept.geometry: The ship is a bold XZ profile spanning 40 mm in Y. A whale silhouette with paired blow jets and a separate crescent are cut vertically through Z, preserving broad perimeter routes and making every internal opening support-free in the intended print orientation.
concept.intended_interaction: Set the broad keel face on a desk to view the ship, then roll the entire one-piece object exactly 90 degrees onto its second stable face and look through the vertical apertures to discover the whale and crescent.
concept.interaction: Stand the flat keel on a desk and view the broad side for the tiny sailing ship crossing one wave. Roll the whole piece 90 degrees onto its second flat face and view from above; ordinary room light makes the whale-and-crescent tunnel read as negative space.
concept.manufacturing: One fused solid, 94 x 40 x 68 mm nominal envelope, flat z=0 print face, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, four walls, no supports, no assembly, and no loose or electronic parts. Minimum deliberate neck is 4 mm.
concept.safety: Ages 14+ desk object; rounded silhouette transitions, no detachable parts, and no sharp functional point. Digital checks do not claim a successful physical print or real-world stability test.
concept.signature_decision: Use two exact orthographic readings of one rigid solid: the held Y-axis view is an unmistakable sailing ship, while a 90-degree roll exposes a Z-through crescent and leaping whale with paired blow jets as negative space.
concept.summary: A palm-sized, one-piece ship silhouette that rolls exactly a quarter-turn to reveal a breaching whale crossing a crescent-moon aperture in the same connected geometry.
concept.title: Moonwake Turn
unresolved_risks: The whale body is somewhat generic without its paired blow jets.
Digital verification does not establish physical print quality, real-world stability, durability, or human response.

research.method: Reference-free original construction grounded in exact orthographic projection and support-free FDM constraints; no external source geometry or purchased component was used.
projection_facts: The ship read is the outer XZ silhouette viewed along Y.
The whale and crescent read is a Z-through aperture viewed along Z after a 90-degree roll.
The two readings therefore come from one immutable solid and ordinary ambient contrast.
